item.title: What Every Music Company Made in Q2 2026 (Updating)
item.description:
[Intro music plays]
Host: "Welcome to our podcast, where we dive into the latest news in the music industry. I'm your host, and today we're talking about the recent earnings reports from music companies. It's been a busy few weeks, with around a dozen publicly traded music companies sharing their results. So, let's dive in and see how they're doing."
[Music transitions to a gentle background tune]
Host: "First up, the major labels. Sony Music is looking strong, with revenue surging 20% year-over-year. Warner Music Group is also seeing double-digit growth, thanks to a big boost in subscription streaming. But Universal Music Group isn't faring as well, with a 25% decline in its share price after disappointing growth margins."
[Short music transition]
Host: "In live music, Live Nation is thriving, with a significant increase in quarterly revenue despite some tough competition from the FIFA World Cup. And Sphere Entertainment is seeing revenue growth from its showings of The Wizard of Oz, although it's still operating at a loss."
[Short music transition]
Host: "Satellite radio giant SiriusXM Holdings is finding its footing with low-cost companion plans and premium channels. And on the streaming front, Spotify is beating growth expectations for premium subscribers and operating income, although it slightly missed its guidance on monthly average users. Deezer is also seeing revenue and adjusted gross profit edge slightly higher."
[Outro music starts playing]
Host: "That's a quick rundown of the latest earnings reports from the music industry. We'll be keeping an eye on the rest of the reports as they come in, so stay tuned for more updates. Thanks for listening, and we'll catch you in the next episode!"
[Outro music continues to play until the end]
